Use case: product-mockup. Asset type: premium architectural photograph for a shower-enclosure catalogue, one square 1254 by 1254 pixel image. Photorealistic bathroom architecture, physically clear simple frameless glass shower construction, restrained precision hardware, soft neutral daylight, tasteful warm stone, no people or clutter. The entire enclosure type must be readable in one photograph, with enough floor visible to understand its layout. Ultra-clear CrystalVision low-iron glass: almost invisible transparent planes, colorless neutral white-gray thin edges, absolutely NO green glass, cyan edge tint, turquoise, blue tint, blue reflections or green ambient light. Reflect warm-neutral room only. Straight plausible corners, hinges and rails attached to real glass; show a coherent installable design with no floating or impossible panels. Minimal accessories: one shower mixer and showerhead, one drain. NO text, dimension lines, labels, arrows, logos, watermarks, drawings, diagrams, exploded view, collage, multiple images, store shelf, catalogue furniture.
Subject: Warm beige limestone bathroom, a rectangular shower recess bounded by three solid stone walls. In the front opening is one single frameless bifold shower door comprised of exactly two equally wide vertical clear glass leaves joined by three compact polished chrome hinges along their shared edge. The whole two-leaf assembly is hinged at the LEFT wall jamb. Show it partly folded INWARD toward the left wall as a compact V shape, with two separate leaves clearly visible at different angles and a wide unobstructed entry across the right two-thirds of the niche. Door has a small chrome pull near its free edge. No sliding rails, no additional fixed front panel, no spurious glass wall behind the folded leaves. Main camera from bathroom at front-right, slight oblique view showing folded door and simple shower niche depth. Shower floor level with bathroom, a slim linear drain along rear wall. Light sand stone, gentle daylight, clean modern room.
assets.visualInspection: Actual image inspected: two inward-folded glass leaves at left, chrome hinge connection, wide entry at right. Targeted edit removed green/cyan glass-edge tint; neutral gray-white edges confirmed.

assets.correctionPrompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Make ONE color correction to this existing bathroom photograph: remove ALL green, teal, cyan, blue and olive tint from every edge and plane of the TWO FOLDED GLASS DOOR LEAVES. Replace the colored glass outlines with neutral dark-to-light gray and silver-white at the same luminance and contrast. The glass must be optically neutral colorless low-iron CrystalVision glass. Preserve exact geometry and image composition, the two inward folded leaves, all hinges and door handle, camera, warm beige wall/floor color, shadows, shower equipment and surrounding room. Do NOT monochrome the whole image. Do NOT change the green plant outside the glass; only neutralize glass edge coloration. Do not add/remove objects or change mechanical geometry. Keep square 1254 px photo, no text.

assets.name: shower-sloped
assets.prompt: Use case: product-mockup. Asset type: premium architectural shower catalogue photograph, square 1254 by 1254 pixels. A simple physically believable shower enclosure inside an ATTIC bathroom beneath one visibly sloping pitched ceiling, low at LEFT and high at RIGHT. Warm light limestone walls and floor, warm off-white plaster sloped ceiling, brushed chrome hardware, soft neutral daylight. The glass front has exactly TWO parts: on the LEFT, one custom-cut fixed clear glass trapezoid whose DIAGONAL TOP EDGE closely follows the sloping ceiling and rises from left to right; on the RIGHT, one ordinary RECTANGULAR hinged glass door with a horizontal top edge and vertical sides. The rectangular door occupies the taller part of the attic and its horizontal top remains BELOW the sloping ceiling, so the door can swing freely; a visibly open air gap exists over the door. The upper-right corner of the left fixed trapezoid meets the door-top height at their vertical junction. Two compact chrome glass-to-glass hinges attach the door to the straight vertical edge of the fixed pane; small chrome pull on free right side, wall channel or clamps secure fixed pane at left. Show the complete front glass shape, the sloped ceiling, the floor and the actual depth of the shower niche from a slightly elevated front-right oblique photographic viewpoint. One showerhead and mixer installed at the high right part of rear wall, linear floor drain. Do not make the door itself trapezoidal or triangular; do not make glass cross through the ceiling. Ultra-clear CrystalVision low-iron glass with neutral white-gray colorless edges, NO green, cyan, teal or blue glass or reflections. No green plants or outdoor greenery; no people, clutter, labels, text, numbers, logos, diagrams, collage, watermark. Photorealistic premium architectural image, coherent simple geometry.
assets.visualInspection: Actual image inspected: sloped attic ceiling, fixed left pane with diagonal upper edge follows ceiling, rectangular right door with horizontal top below ceiling, two hinges at vertical junction. Neutral glass edges, coherent geometry.
